text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bloody weekend: more than 80 people, mostly women and children, slaughtered by "terrorists". The worst massacre occured in Thalit hamlet, in Medea province, where all the 52 inhabitants were killed.

- Algeria's foreign currency reserves reached $5.3 billion in March, the equivalent of six months of imports. Inflation continues its decline to reach less than 10 percent in February, its lowest level for a decade.

- Journalists, who are candidates for the parliamentary elections, will be barred from covering the election campaign. Government ministers, competing for parliamentary seats, will get no media exposure for their official activities.
- Fifty-two villagers massacred in a hamlet in Medea province.
- A cluster of good economic figures over falling inflation, higher foreign currency reserves and trade balance surplus increases are the results of reforms undertaken by President Liamine Zeroual.
